title: Wa mā adrāka & wa mā yudrīka — what follows the question?
Almost the same
in English.
beats.narration: What's the difference between wa mā adrāka and wa mā yudrīka in the Quran? In English, they're translated almost identically: What could make you know?
captions: wa mā adrāka and wa mā yudrīka?

beats.eyebrow: A PATTERN NOTED BY SUFYAN IBN ‘UYAYNAH
title: Watch what
comes next.
beats.narration: But the scholar Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah pointed out a difference: Whenever Allah says wa mā adrāka, He gives an explanation. With wa mā yudrīka, that specific answer isn't given. Listen to these examples.
captions: Wa mā adrāka: He gives an explanation.
Wa mā yudrīka: that answer isn’t given.

title: What is the
Night of Decree?
beats.narration: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ What can make you know what the Night of Decree is?
captions: what the Night of Decree is?

title: Better than
1,000 months.
arabic: لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ
beats.narration: The next verse explains: لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.
captions: The Night of Decree is better

title: What is the
night visitor?
beats.narration: And again: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الطَّارِقُ What can make you know what the night visitor is?

title: Now listen to
wa mā yudrīka.
beats.narration: Both times, an explanation follows. Now compare wa mā yudrīka:

beats.eyebrow: THE EXACT TIME ISN’T GIVEN • AL-AHZAB 33:63
title: Perhaps the Hour
is near.
arabic: وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّ السَّاعَةَ تَكُونُ قَرِيبًا
beats.narration: وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّ السَّاعَةَ تَكُونُ قَرِيبًا What would make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near. We're told it may be near. We aren't told when.
captions: We’re told it may be near.

title: Perhaps he might
be purified.
beats.narration: And: وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكَّىٰ What would make you know? Perhaps he might be purified. A possibility is mentioned. His outcome isn't confirmed there.

beats.eyebrow: NEXT TIME YOU HEAR THESE PHRASES…
title: An explanation.
Or an open question.
beats.narration: So next time you hear these phrases, listen closely: Wa mā adrāka, an explanation follows. Wa mā yudrīka, the specific answer isn't revealed.
captions: Wa mā adrāka: an explanation follows.
Wa mā yudrīka: the answer isn’t revealed.

beats.eyebrow: SIMILAR IN ENGLISH. DIFFERENT IN USE.
title: Two expressions.
Different endings.
beats.narration: Two expressions that can sound similar in English, but watch how differently the Quran uses them.
captions: They can sound similar in English…
